const ans = `IDEA: HORO-LEAF-CERT
TITLE: Horospherical deepest-level SID re-assignment certified by Gromov delta: a precision-first leaf move rule for the frozen RQ-VAE
MOTIVATION: The previous certificate-guarded split/merge moved about one third of the catalogue because its admissible predicate was necessary but not sufficient: every item that satisfied it still had several "equally acceptable" destinations, so the tie-break, not the evidence, decided the SID. The leaf level is where that damage lands: it is the token that disambiguates two items that share levels 1..L-1, so a mass leaf move both creates new collisions and destroys the leaf-token conditional entropy that a generative recommender needs. This idea replaces the tie-break with a distortion-budget margin measured on the frozen Stage-2 geometry, so a leaf item moves only when the geometry resolves the destination beyond its own noise floor.
NOVELTY: No mechanism here uses horospherical / Busemann (ideal-boundary) geometry; prior work used Poincare distance, radii, Frechet centroids, per-level curvature feedback and cone/prefix variants. The secondary novelty is the sufficiency test: a *unique* Busemann argmax whose margin exceeds 2*delta_p, where delta_p is the Gromov delta of the frozen Poincare embedding of the item's training behaviour neighbourhood. delta is measured, not chosen, so the move rule needs no swept constant, and ties resolve to "do not move" instead of to a coverage-increasing tie-break.
CHANGE: After Stage 2, only the level-L code c_L(x) may change, and only inside x's own prefix group. A move x -> k is applied iff a two-sided Gromov-delta certificate holds AND k is the unique argmax of a Busemann alignment score by more than twice the group's measured distortion budget AND the total leaf-slot Gromov delta of the partition strictly falls.
SPECIFICATION: (1) Freeze Stage-2 encoder embeddings u_x, level-L centres e_k, SIDs s(x); compute sigma = median_x ||u_x - mean(u)|| and map z_x = tanh(||u_x-mean(u)||/sigma)*unit(u_x-mean(u)) into the unit ball, curvature kappa = -1/sigma^2. (2) From TRAIN sessions only build directed counts w(x,y); behavioural star N(x) = top-mass successors + top-mass predecessors + {x}. (3) Compute delta(S) by the four-point Gromov product in the curved metric; set delta_p = median over the prefix group of delta(N(x)). (4) For every level-L slot k build the leave-one-out ideal points xi_out(k), xi_in(k) from successor and predecessor mass. (5) Score A(x,k) = b_xi_out(z_x) + b_xi_in(z_x) with the Busemann function of the ball. (6) For each item take the behaviour-bounded candidate set K_x, apply the certificate, the unique-margin test, the partition-descent test and the occupancy cap, accept in descending margin, one pass, no iteration. (7) Write the new SIDs; run the frozen Stage 3 (150 epochs) unchanged.
COST: Zero added optimiser steps during Stage 2 (the pass runs once after epoch 3000, before Stage 3) and zero added parameters. One-time pass: about 2.5e5 Busemann evaluations of O(d<=256) (~6e7 flops) and about 1.7e7 Gromov triples over stars of ~7-17 items (~1e8 flops), i.e. seconds to a few minutes vectorised on CPU; caches about 50 MB. At the frozen scale that is 0 FLOPs/step over the 72,000 steps (24 steps x 3000 epochs), under 1e-6 of Stage-2 compute, and Stage 3 stays at 150 epochs.
HYPOTHESIS: Within-prefix leaf tokens become behaviourally homogeneous where the frozen geometry can resolve it, so the Stage-3 leaf-token conditional entropy falls and test_recall@10 rises; observable as a small moved fraction, a strictly lower mean per-item deepest-code conditional entropy, a bit-identical validation L1 negative hit rate, and recall@10 above 0.065.
RISKS: delta_p may be large, emptying the move set (null result); the descent test is size-monotone in delta, so it may under-move or bias toward splits; if the frozen leaf geometry is already behaviour-aligned the Busemann gain is real but useless; a single run cannot separate seed noise from effect.
BEHAVIOR SIGNAL: Directed item transitions from the training split, aggregated into per-item successor and predecessor distributions and into a behaviour "star" neighbourhood.
BEHAVIOR COMPUTATION: w(x,y) = count of consecutive (item_t, item_{t+1}) pairs inside TRAIN sessions; N1(x) = smallest set of highest-w successors covering at least half of x's outgoing mass (m derived from the mass, not chosen); N1^-(x) likewise for incoming; N(x) = N1(x) union N1^-(x) union {x}; slot star N(k) = union of N(a) for a in k; slot ideal directions Dout_k = sum_{a in k} sum_y w(a,y) u_y and Din_k = sum_{a in k} sum_y w(y,a) u_y.
LEAKAGE BOUNDARY: w, N(.), delta_p, the descent objective and the capacity cap are all read from the TRAIN split only; u_x, e_k and the prefix codes are frozen Stage-2 outputs trained on the same training interactions; the pass runs once, after Stage 2 ends and before Stage 3 starts, and no validation or test interaction is ever read. Validation is used only to print the L1 negative hit rate and the entropy diagnostics, never as an accept condition.
HYPERBOLIC OPERATOR: The Busemann function b_xi(z) = log((1-||z||^2)/||z-xi||^2) of the Poincare ball at ideal point xi on the boundary, with trainable-free curvature kappa = -1/sigma^2, sigma = median Stage-2 embedding norm (measured); b_xi is normalised to b_xi(0) = 0 and equals the full radius d(0,z) exactly when z lies on the geodesic ray to xi. The Gromov delta uses the Mobius (Poincare) distance d_H(a,b) = 2 artanh ||(-a) + b||.
HYPERBOLIC LOCATION: In the deepest-level quantization step of the frozen RQ-VAE: the assignment of c_L, evaluated in the Poincare ball into which the frozen item embeddings are pushed by exp_0 at curvature kappa. Levels 1..L-1 are not recomputed.
COUPLING PATH: TRAIN transitions -> per-item behaviour star -> Gromov delta of the frozen curved embedding of that star -> delta_p distortion budget -> ideal points xi of each leaf slot from successor/predecessor mass -> Busemann alignment A(x,k) -> unique-margin acceptance -> c_L(x) -> Stage 3 recall. Behaviour supplies xi and delta_p; geometry supplies b_xi and d_H; either removal changes the argmax and therefore the SID.
COUPLING EQUATION: A(x,k) = b_{xi_out(k,-x)}(z_x) + b_{xi_in(k,-x)}(z_x), with xi_out(k) = unit(sum_{a in k} sum_y w(a,y) u_y), z_x = exp_0^{kappa}(u_x), and acceptance requiring A(x,k) - max_{j != k} A(x,j) > 2 delta_p, where delta_p = median_{x in p} Gromov_delta_H(N(x)).
OBSERVABLES: moved fraction of the 24556 items; validation L1 negative hit rate before/after (must be bit-identical because level 1 is untouched, and any drift is a bug signal); per-item deepest-code conditional entropy H_L(x) before/after (mean, median, fraction decreased); counts of each rejection reason (split certificate, merge certificate, margin, descent, capacity); Stage-3 test_recall@10.
ABLATION BEHAVIOR OFF: xi_out(k) = xi_in(k) = unit(e_k) (direction of the frozen level-L centroid), so A reduces to a purely geometric horospherical alignment and w never enters; delta_p and the certificate stay unchanged.
ABLATION GEOMETRY OFF: kappa -> 0, so d_H becomes the Euclidean distance, delta_p is measured in the Euclidean metric, and b_xi degenerates to the linear projection 2<log_0 z_x, xi>; the identical acceptance logic then runs without curvature.
ABLATION BOTH ON: the full coupled rule above, with behaviour-derived ideal points and the curved Busemann/delta quantities, run once.
SPEC EQUATIONS:
sigma = median_x ||u_x - mean(u)||;  z_x = tanh(||u_x-mean(u)||/sigma) * (u_x-mean(u))/||u_x-mean(u)||
kappa = -1/sigma^2;  d_H(a,b) = 2 artanh( ||(-a) (+) b|| )
w(x,y) = #{(t,t+1): item_t=x, item_{t+1}=y in TRAIN};  N(x) = N1(x) U N1^-(x) U {x};  N(k) = U_{a in k} N(a)
<a,b> = (d_H(0,a)+d_H(0,b)-d_H(a,b))/2;  delta(S) = max_{a,b,c in S} [ <a,b> - min(<a,c>,<b,c>) ]_+
delta_p = median_{x in p} delta(N(x))
Dout_k = sum_{a in k} sum_y w(a,y) u_y;  Din_k = sum_{a in k} sum_y w(y,a) u_y;  xi = D/||D||
Dout_{k,-x} = Dout_k - sum_y w(x,y) u_y if x in k
b_xi(z) = log( (1-||z||^2) / ||z-xi||^2 );  A(x,k) = b_{xi_out(k,-x)}(z_x) + b_{xi_in(k,-x)}(z_x)
K_x = { c_L(y) : y in N1(x) U N1^-(x) } minus {c_L(x)}, same prefix group only
CERT_split(x): delta(N(k_x minus {x})) <= delta_p ;  CERT_merge(x,k): delta(N(k) U N(x)) <= delta_p
PREC_margin(x,k): A(x,k) - max_{j in K_x, j != k} A(x,j) > 2 delta_p  AND  A(x,k) - A(x,k_x) > 2 delta_p
PREC_descent(x,k): [delta(N(k_x minus {x})) + delta(N(k U {x}))] - [delta(N(k_x)) + delta(N(k))] < 0
PREC_capacity(x,k): |k| + 1 <= cap_p, cap_p = max_{j in p} |j| in the frozen Stage-2 partition
accept(x) = all five; apply in descending A(x,k*) - A(x,k_x); one move per item; single pass
SPEC INPUTS OUTPUTS: Inputs: frozen Stage-2 u_x, e_k, s(x); TRAIN transition counts; the prefix groups. Outputs: the new level-L code c_L'(x) for a subset of items, the moved fraction, the rejection-reason counts, and the before/after diagnostics. No parameter or gradient is produced; the emitted object is the SID table consumed by Stage 3.
SAFEGUARDS: clamp delta at 0; skip slots with ||Dout_k|| or ||Din_k|| below 1e-12 or with no observed successors/predecessors; guard artanh with the argument clipped to 1-1e-7; clamp ||z|| <= 1-1e-7; if a prefix group has fewer than 4 items with a non-trivial star, fall back to the global median delta_p; treat NaN/Inf in A as -inf so the item never moves; reject a move whose target slot is empty-of-behaviour (no xi) ; enforce the capacity cap so no slot can exceed the group's own Stage-2 maximum occupancy; deterministic tie handling (descending margin, then ascending item id); assert the L1 negative hit rate is bit-identical after the pass.
END IDEA`;
const r = await tools.progress.append_progress({content: "STAGE 2 — final answer (complete block, stands alone).\n\n" + ans});
return r;

NOVELTY: No mechanism here uses horospherical / Busemann (ideal-boundary) geometry; prior work used Poincare distance, radii, Frechet centroids, per-level curvature feedback and cone/prefix variants. The secondary novelty is the sufficiency test: a *unique* Busemann argmax whose margin exceeds 2*delta_p, where delta_p is the Gromov delta of the frozen Poincare embedding of the item's training behaviour neighbourhood. delta is measured, not chosen, so the move rule needs no swept constant, and ties resolve to "do not move" instead of to a coverage-increasing tie-break.
CHANGE: After Stage 2, only the level-L code c_L(x) may change, and only inside x's own prefix group. A move x -> k is applied iff a two-sided Gromov-delta certificate holds AND k is the unique argmax of a Busemann alignment score by more than twice the group's measured distortion budget AND the total leaf-slot Gromov delta of the partition strictly falls.
SPECIFICATION: (1) Freeze Stage-2 encoder embeddings u_x, level-L centres e_k, SIDs s(x); compute sigma = median_x ||u_x - mean(u)|| and map z_x = tanh(||u_x-mean(u)||/sigma)*unit(u_x-mean(u)) into the unit ball, curvature kappa = -1/sigma^2. (2) From TRAIN sessions only build directed counts w(x,y); behavioural star N(x) = top-mass successors + top-mass predecessors + {x}. (3) Compute delta(S) by the four-point Gromov product in the curved metric; set delta_p = median over the prefix group of delta(N(x)). (4) For every level-L slot k build the leave-one-out ideal points xi_out(k), xi_in(k) from successor and predecessor mass. (5) Score A(x,k) = b_xi_out(z_x) + b_xi_in(z_x) with the Busemann function of the ball. (6) For each item take the behaviour-bounded candidate set K_x, apply the certificate, the unique-margin test, the partition-descent test and the occupancy cap, accept in descending margin, one pass, no iteration. (7) Write the new SIDs; run the frozen Stage 3 (150 epochs) unchanged.
COST: Zero added optimiser steps during Stage 2 (the pass runs once after epoch 3000, before Stage 3) and zero added parameters. One-time pass: about 2.5e5 Busemann evaluations of O(d<=256) (~6e7 flops) and about 1.7e7 Gromov triples over stars of ~7-17 items (~1e8 flops), i.e. seconds to a few minutes vectorised on CPU; caches about 50 MB. At the frozen scale that is 0 FLOPs/step over the 72,000 steps (24 steps x 3000 epochs), under 1e-6 of Stage-2 compute, and Stage 3 stays at 150 epochs.
HYPOTHESIS: Within-prefix leaf tokens become behaviourally homogeneous where the frozen geometry can resolve it, so the Stage-3 leaf-token conditional entropy falls and test_recall@10 rises; observable as a small moved fraction, a strictly lower mean per-item deepest-code conditional entropy, a bit-identical validation L1 negative hit rate, and recall@10 above 0.065.
RISKS: delta_p may be large, emptying the move set (null result); the descent test is size-monotone in delta, so it may under-move or bias toward splits; if the frozen leaf geometry is already behaviour-aligned the Busemann gain is real but useless; a single run cannot separate seed noise from effect.
BEHAVIOR SIGNAL: Directed item transitions from the training split, aggregated into per-item successor and predecessor distributions and into a behaviour "star" neighbourhood.
BEHAVIOR COMPUTATION: w(x,y) = count of consecutive (item_t, item_{t+1}) pairs inside TRAIN sessions; N1(x) = smallest set of highest-w successors covering at least half of x's outgoing mass (m derived from the mass, not chosen); N1^-(x) likewise for incoming; N(x) = N1(x) union N1^-(x) union {x}; slot star N(k) = union of N(a) for a in k; slot ideal directions Dout_k = sum_{a in k} sum_y w(a,y) u_y and Din_k = sum_{a in k} sum_y w(y,a) u_y.
LEAKAGE BOUNDARY: w, N(.), delta_p, the descent objective and the capacity cap are all read from the TRAIN split only; u_x, e_k and the prefix codes are frozen Stage-2 outputs trained on the same training interactions; the pass runs once, after Stage 2 ends and before Stage 3 starts, and no validation or test interaction is ever read. Validation is used only to print the L1 negative hit rate and the entropy diagnostics, never as an accept condition.
HYPERBOLIC OPERATOR: The Busemann function b_xi(z) = log((1-||z||^2)/||z-xi||^2) of the Poincare ball at ideal point xi on the boundary, with trainable-free curvature kappa = -1/sigma^2, sigma = median Stage-2 embedding norm (measured); b_xi is normalised to b_xi(0) = 0 and equals the full radius d(0,z) exactly when z lies on the geodesic ray to xi. The Gromov delta uses the Mobius (Poincare) distance d_H(a,b) = 2 artanh ||(-a) + b||.
HYPERBOLIC LOCATION: In the deepest-level quantization step of the frozen RQ-VAE: the assignment of c_L, evaluated in the Poincare ball into which the frozen item embeddings are pushed by exp_0 at curvature kappa. Levels 1..L-1 are not recomputed.
COUPLING PATH: TRAIN transitions -> per-item behaviour star -> Gromov delta of the frozen curved embedding of that star -> delta_p distortion budget -> ideal points xi of each leaf slot from successor/predecessor mass -> Busemann alignment A(x,k) -> unique-margin acceptance -> c_L(x) -> Stage 3 recall. Behaviour supplies xi and delta_p; geometry supplies b_xi and d_H; either removal changes the argmax and therefore the SID.
COUPLING EQUATION: A(x,k) = b_{xi_out(k,-x)}(z_x) + b_{xi_in(k,-x)}(z_x), with xi_out(k) = unit(sum_{a in k} sum_y w(a,y) u_y), z_x = exp_0^{kappa}(u_x), and acceptance requiring A(x,k) - max_{j != k} A(x,j) > 2 delta_p, where delta_p = median_{x in p} Gromov_delta_H(N(x)).
OBSERVABLES: moved fraction of the 24556 items; validation L1 negative hit rate before/after (must be bit-identical because level 1 is untouched, and any drift is a bug signal); per-item deepest-code conditional entropy H_L(x) before/after (mean, median, fraction decreased); counts of each rejection reason (split certificate, merge certificate, margin, descent, capacity); Stage-3 test_recall@10.
ABLATION BEHAVIOR OFF: xi_out(k) = xi_in(k) = unit(e_k) (direction of the frozen level-L centroid), so A reduces to a purely geometric horospherical alignment and w never enters; delta_p and the certificate stay unchanged.
ABLATION GEOMETRY OFF: kappa -> 0, so d_H becomes the Euclidean distance, delta_p is measured in the Euclidean metric, and b_xi degenerates to the linear projection 2<log_0 z_x, xi>; the identical acceptance logic then runs without curvature.
ABLATION BOTH ON: the full coupled rule above, with behaviour-derived ideal points and the curved Busemann/delta quantities, run once.
SPEC EQUATIONS:
sigma = median_x ||u_x - mean(u)||;  z_x = tanh(||u_x-mean(u)||/sigma) * (u_x-mean(u))/||u_x-mean(u)||
kappa = -1/sigma^2;  d_H(a,b) = 2 artanh( ||(-a) (+) b|| )
w(x,y) = #{(t,t+1): item_t=x, item_{t+1}=y in TRAIN};  N(x) = N1(x) U N1^-(x) U {x};  N(k) = U_{a in k} N(a)
<a,b> = (d_H(0,a)+d_H(0,b)-d_H(a,b))/2;  delta(S) = max_{a,b,c in S} [ <a,b> - min(<a,c>,<b,c>) ]_+
delta_p = median_{x in p} delta(N(x))
Dout_k = sum_{a in k} sum_y w(a,y) u_y;  Din_k = sum_{a in k} sum_y w(y,a) u_y;  xi = D/||D||
Dout_{k,-x} = Dout_k - sum_y w(x,y) u_y if x in k
b_xi(z) = log( (1-||z||^2) / ||z-xi||^2 );  A(x,k) = b_{xi_out(k,-x)}(z_x) + b_{xi_in(k,-x)}(z_x)
K_x = { c_L(y) : y in N1(x) U N1^-(x) } minus {c_L(x)}, same prefix group only
CERT_split(x): delta(N(k_x minus {x})) <= delta_p ;  CERT_merge(x,k): delta(N(k) U N(x)) <= delta_p
PREC_margin(x,k): A(x,k) - max_{j in K_x, j != k} A(x,j) > 2 delta_p  AND  A(x,k) - A(x,k_x) > 2 delta_p
PREC_descent(x,k): [delta(N(k_x minus {x})) + delta(N(k U {x}))] - [delta(N(k_x)) + delta(N(k))] < 0
PREC_capacity(x,k): |k| + 1 <= cap_p, cap_p = max_{j in p} |j| in the frozen Stage-2 partition
accept(x) = all five; apply in descending A(x,k*) - A(x,k_x); one move per item; single pass
SPEC INPUTS OUTPUTS: Inputs: frozen Stage-2 u_x, e_k, s(x); TRAIN transition counts; the prefix groups. Outputs: the new level-L code c_L'(x) for a subset of items, the moved fraction, the rejection-reason counts, and the before/after diagnostics. No parameter or gradient is produced; the emitted object is the SID table consumed by Stage 3.
SAFEGUARDS: clamp delta at 0; skip slots with ||Dout_k|| or ||Din_k|| below 1e-12 or with no observed successors/predecessors; guard artanh with the argument clipped to 1-1e-7; clamp ||z|| <= 1-1e-7; if a prefix group has fewer than 4 items with a non-trivial star, fall back to the global median delta_p; treat NaN/Inf in A as -inf so the item never moves; reject a move whose target slot is empty-of-behaviour (no xi) ; enforce the capacity cap so no slot can exceed the group's own Stage-2 maximum occupancy; deterministic tie handling (descending margin, then ascending item id); assert the L1 negative hit rate is bit-identical after the pass.
END IDEA`;
